A made-up relation has no property to contradict. The instance places are real; the pairs are arbitrary, so no stored fact pairs them.

notes: Dev RBox expansion, paired with geography-replace-d006: that revision makes 'is the antipode of' asymmetric; this record gives a made-up relation the same property (asymmetry), applied to real places (fictional: relation, as README prescribes for RBox expansion). cairn_bound_to is catalogued in staging/geography.RELATIONS.md as fictional with no property tags; the insert makes it asymmetric. The earlier version made a different made-up relation (has_cairn_port) functional, which did not match the property the revision changes. Instance wording follows the revision, which also balances yes and no: the direct question asks 'asymmetric' (yes), the first instance asks whether the converse follows (no), the second whether the fact rules the converse out (yes); the zh query asks the first instance and the es query the second, so the record has 3 yes and 2 no. The pairs (Trondheim and Valparaiso, Hobart and Reykjavik) are arbitrary real places, so nothing real settles the converse, and 'cairn-bound' has no built-in direction, so a model cannot answer from the name: Wikipedia search finds nothing under either spelling. Asymmetry is the edited property here, not a derivation, as in the revision (CRITERIA Rule 12 lists asymmetry as not used for derivations; the instance answers do change from 'no property' to a definite one, so the logic holds; flagged as a spec note). The side facts are the revision's (same facts, same evidence). Near unrelated asks the same property of a real geography relation (a leak would turn its 'no' into 'yes'); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation. hops counts the instance fact in the prompt as the bridge, as the other RBox records do. The infini-gram API was blocking this machine on 2026-11-12, so the made-up name has Wikipedia searches only and no corpus count.
